display_name: TimescaleDB (self-hosted extension) / Tiger Cloud (formerly Timescale Cloud)

default_port_notes.5432: PRIMARY — standard Postgres wire protocol, self-hosted/Docker default. Extension rides the same port as vanilla Postgres; port alone is NOT a fingerprint.
default_port_notes.11111: Tiger Cloud direct-connection service port (non-standard, cloud-managed only) — UNVERIFIED exact value, needs direct doc-fetch confirmation, see research_questions.

auth_default: INHERITED FROM POSTGRES — zero bundled auth layer. Extension adds no authentication logic of its own; hooks into the Postgres executor/planner only. Self-hosted Docker image (timescale/timescaledb*): if POSTGRES_PASSWORD is unset at container init, password checks are disabled for ALL users (trust-equivalent) — inherited from the postgres:latest base image behavior, not TimescaleDB-specific. Tiger Cloud (managed) defaults to scram-sha-256 + TLS-required.
auth_config_env: PGDATA — data directory (affects pg_hba.conf persistence across restarts if bind-mounted)
TIMESCALEDB_TELEMETRY — telemetry on/off (relevant to CVE-2023-25149 trigger surface, not an auth control)
default_creds: postgres:postgres (anecdotal, unverified — common Docker-Compose footgun pattern, not a vendor default)
install_tell: docker run -p 5432:5432 timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg16 (or -ha variant); presence of shared_preload_libraries = 'timescaledb' in postgresql.conf if readable
misconfig_patterns: Docker container run without POSTGRES_PASSWORD set -> full trust auth, any TCP client with network reach gets superuser
-p 5432:5432 bound to 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1 in compose files -> direct internet exposure, inherited verbatim from postgres:latest

CVE-2023-25149 / CVE-2026-29089 class: telemetry job or extension-upgrade running with unlocked search_path -> low-priv authenticated user who can CREATE FUNCTION on a privileged job's search_path rides it to superuser-context execution
timescaledb_information.jobs enumeration reveals continuous-aggregate/compression job owners and proc_schema -> check for user-writable schemas on any privileged job's search_path

passive: No pre-auth banner tell exists — Postgres wire protocol gives no extension manifest before authentication succeeds
Docker-image-layer tell (registry/compose scrape only): image name timescale/timescaledb* or timescale/timescaledb-ha:pg<N>

response_markers: SELECT extname, extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'timescaledb'
SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.hypertables (v2.x; v1.x uses singular timescaledb_information.hypertable)
active_probe.false_positive_check: Try both singular (v1.x) and plural (v2.x) timescaledb_information table names to bracket major-version detection.

version_router.pre_auth: Not possible — hard blocker distinguishing TimescaleDB from HTTP-native platforms that leak version/schema pre-auth.
version_router.post_auth: pg_extension.extversion gives exact TimescaleDB version once connected.

shodan_dorks.basic_all_lines: product:PostgreSQL (0% precision alone — matches entire Postgres population, cannot distinguish TimescaleDB)
shodan_dorks.cloud_speculative: product:PostgreSQL port:11111 (UNVERIFIED — Tiger Cloud port value not confirmed via direct doc-fetch)
shodan_dorks.cloud_hostname: hostname:"tsdb.cloud.timescale.com" (cert/hostname-field match, not http.html — test against Shodan web UI per Step 0 mechanism)

engine_routing.shodan_visible: None — no HTTP body exists to banner. Structural limiter vs HTTP-native AI/vector-DB targets.
engine_routing.censys_only: Same limiter applies; Censys TLS cert SAN indexing may catch *.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com hostnames where Shodan misses them.

deployment_tells: Docker image name pattern timescale/timescaledb[-ha]:*-pg<14|15|16|17|18> in any exposed compose/Dockerfile/CI config
Cloud-managed: hostname suffix *.tsdb.cloud.timescale.com, non-standard ports (11111 / pooler ranges — unverified exact values)
shared_preload_libraries = 'timescaledb' in postgresql.conf if config file readable via misconfigured backup/volume exposure
Presence of timescaledb_information, _timescaledb_internal, _timescaledb_catalog schemas visible post-auth via \dn
pivot_paths: timescaledb_information.hypertables -> full enumeration of time-series tables, dimension columns, chunk intervals (schema-only, no row read)
timescaledb_information.continuous_aggregates -> pre-computed rollup names often descriptive (daily_revenue_agg, hourly_sensor_avg) — names ARE the finding
timescaledb_information.jobs + job_stats -> background job introspection, potential search_path-hijack pivot
_timescaledb_catalog.hypertable / dimension -> lower-level catalog internals for cross-major-version fingerprinting
Standard Postgres pivots apply unchanged: pg_roles, information_schema.tables, pg_stat_activity, dblink/postgres_fdw if installed
vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-25149 (GHSA / Snyk SNYK-UNMANAGED-TIMESCALETIMESCALEDB-3319678): privilege escalation via unlocked search_path in built-in telemetry collection job. Affects 2.8.0-2.9.2. Low-priv user plants function the telemetry job executes, escalating to job's elevated privilege. Fixed 2.9.3.

CVE-2026-29089 (GHSA-vgp2-jj5c-828m): arbitrary code execution via search_path manipulation shadowing built-in Postgres functions during extension upgrade. Affects 2.23.0-2.25.1. CVSS 8.8 (High/Critical). Low-priv user -> superuser. Fixed 2.25.2.

PATTERN INSIGHT: both extension-specific CVEs are the same vulnerability class — untrusted/unlocked search_path during a privileged background operation (telemetry job / extension upgrade). Any TimescaleDB instance where non-superuser roles can CREATE FUNCTION in a schema on a privileged job's search_path is a live escalation path independent of the specific CVE/version boundary.
auth_default_thesis: REFUTES the category thesis for managed cloud, CONFIRMS it for unhardened self-hosted. TimescaleDB inherits Postgres's auth model wholesale — no bundled auth layer of its own — so auth-off-default holds exactly to the degree the underlying Postgres deployment does. Self-hosted Docker images carry the well-documented POSTGRES_PASSWORD-unset-means-trust-auth footgun, making auth-off-default a real and common state there. Tiger Cloud (managed) diverges and defaults to hardened scram-sha-256+TLS — the thesis is refuted for the managed variant. Structurally distinct from the rest of the category: no pre-auth HTTP fingerprint exists at all, which caps this platform's contribution to population-scale Shodan/Censys harvest regardless of auth posture.
